followups.detail: Count-based cursor (agent_watch.py:1985-1987, len(lines)>cursor) vs the shifting lines[-500:] window (agent_watch.py:722, _OUTPUT_BACKFILL_LIMIT=500) means once a spawn exceeds 500 output lines len(lines) plateaus at 500 while the window shifts forward, so the tail freezes at the first 500-line window and drops later chunks. Use a content/seq identity anchor instead of len().

body.summary: Fresh-context audit of P30-I20-W58 (commit d0ef1bb1) against its 2 criteria. Both hold. CR-01 (open watch tail picks up newly-persisted chunks each poll tick): the fix hoists _sync_output_from_store (agent_watch.py:1945) into the state-reactive poll-backstop watcher _on_app_state (agent_watch.py:2019), registered at :1891, calling it UNCONDITIONALLY before the parity early-exit at :2021 -- pre-W58 the tail only backfilled on mount and same-fleet poll ticks hit the early-exit. Sync reads persisted agent.output.chunk lines off the event store, independent of live daemon push. Test test_agent_watch_tail_syncs_new_chunks_from_store_on_poll (test_modes_agent_watch.py:562) passes. CR-02 (store sync + live push never double-render): per-recompose count cursor (agent_watch.py:1775 reset; :1985-1987 advance) plus OutputTail.replace clearing all prior rows incl live-push (output_tail.py:257) on first content sync, plus append_output gated off once store owns the tail (:2129-2130). All 3 refutation orderings (push-then-sync, sync-then-push, cap-shift edge) fail to produce a duplicate. Tests test_output_tail_replace_clears_prior_rows_and_reseeds + poll test (asserts count==1) pass. Verdict pass-with-followups because refutation surfaced one genuine latent defect not covered by either criterion for bounded output.

One collateral regression: the wave relocated the run_close_preflight call from mutate() into the new _mutate_wave_close() without updating tests/workflow/verify/test_preflight.py::test_daemon_close_pipeline_calls_run_close_preflight, which asserts `await run_close_preflight(` and the injected seams live in inspect.getsource(daemon_state.mutate); that test passed before the wave and now fails, so the committed suite is red until it is repointed at _mutate_wave_close. Functional deliverable is correct; the stale introspection test is a required follow-up before iter/phase close.

criteria.criterion: Stamp session_id on RuntimeBaseline and RuntimeLatest
bump schema_version 1.14 to 1.15
add the v1_14_to_v1_15 migration backfilling session_id as null
regenerate the golden state schema
A runtime.capture arriving from a session other than the baseline session folds the prior session total into an accumulated origin and rebases
a wave spanning N sessions sums N per-session runtimes instead of differencing mismatched origins
_counter_delta never observes a backwards counter on the interactive path
a wave claimed in one session and closed in another closes cleanly instead of raising LifecycleError
A wave claimed in a Claude Code session
left CLAIMED across a Stop boundary
and closed in a later turn records elapsed_eu greater than 0 with harness=claude-code and a non-null model

refutations: Residual (non-blocking, non-regressing): _rebase_for_session's adopt branch (state.py:2813 - baseline.session_id is None and wave.runtime_latest is None) restamps a pre-1.15 baseline with the capturing session_id while retaining its non-zero counters. If that baseline was captured mid-session A (non-zero counters) and the first-ever capture arrives from a genuinely different session B whose cumulative counters are lower, close-time compute_runtime_delta -> _counter_delta sees latest_B < baseline and raises LifecycleError. This narrows criterion 7's literal 'never'. Scope is limited to pre-1.15 waves claimed-but-not-yet-captured that cross a session boundary during the upgrade window; post-1.15 waves always carry baseline.session_id and take the correct fold/rebase path, and the failure is identical to the pre-W27 bug (no regression). Follow-up: prefer the zero-rebase (fold) path over restamp-in-place for the null-session ambiguous case, or clamp the delta, so the legacy edge also closes cleanly.
body.summary: Cross-session runtime rebasing is implemented correctly and well-tested. session_id is stamped on RuntimeBaseline (inherited by RuntimeLatest) and plumbed end-to-end (hook runner.py:303-305 -> RuntimeCaptureParams.session_id -> _runtime_latest_from_params -> _capture_runtime_baseline -> headless snapshots in agent.py). schema_version advances 1.14->1.15 with a registered, idempotent v1_14_to_v1_15 migration backfilling session_id:null and runtime_carry:null; _DEFAULT_TARGET_VERSION and the Literal set move in lockstep, and both golden schema copies (src/ + docs/) were regenerated. runtime_capture calls _rebase_for_session before merging, folding the finished session's clamped-at-zero total into Wave.runtime_carry and rebasing the baseline onto the new session's zero origin, so compute_runtime_delta (now carry-aware across close, fleet lane spend, and the cost overlay) sums N per-session runtimes instead of differencing mismatched origins. The interactive same-session path (Stop boundary within one session) never rebases, so latest>=baseline and the close records elapsed_eu>0 with harness=claude-code and a transcript-derived non-null model. All 231 targeted tests pass. One narrow, non-regressing follow-up: the legacy adopt branch keeps a pre-1.15 baseline's non-zero counters while restamping the capturing session, so a genuinely-cross-session first capture with lower new-session counters could still trip _counter_delta -- affects only pre-1.15 claimed waves in transit and does not regress prior behavior.

criteria.criterion: The carry records which sessions it has already folded so two interleaved sessions on the same wave cannot fold the same session twice and cannot double-count its runtime
A session that ends without a capture does not silently lose its runtime nor inflate the folded-session count
The rebased origin is the new session's counters at the moment the wave is resumed rather than zero so work the operator did in that session before touching the wave is not charged to it
Regression tests pin the interleaved-session case and the no-capture case which the shipped code both got wrong

refutations: Criterion 1 literal wording is not met: RuntimeCarry does not record WHICH sessions it folded (only an integer sessions_folded). Double-counting is prevented by re-originating the baseline on the incoming session's counters, not by a folded-session id set. The mechanism is sound for runtime (monotonic within-session counters mean the advanced baseline never re-folds already-counted work, pinned by test_returning_to_an_earlier_session_does_not_double_count_it), but sessions_folded counts stints not distinct sessions: a deeper interleave A->B->A->B increments it once per transition (would read 3 for 2 distinct sessions), so the audit-trail count can over-report. Non-blocking followup, no runtime error.

Out-of-criteria observation (W37 code in the same audit range, not one of W36's four criteria): _reorigin_on_reset re-origins ALL counter fields to the incoming snapshot even when only one counter regressed (e.g. duration basis change while token counters kept growing), which zeroes the delta for the non-regressed token counters accrued this session up to the reset, under-counting tokens/cost at close. Belongs to W37's success criteria, flagged for completeness.
body.summary: W36's cross-session rebase fix is substantively correct and the four criteria are met and pinned by tests. The rebase now re-origins the baseline on the incoming session's counters (not zero), so the interleaved A->B->A case no longer double-counts (test_returning_to_an_earlier_session_does_not_double_count_it asserts 1500 not 2700), a resumed session's pre-wave work is excluded (test_new_session_origin_excludes_work_the_wave_did_not_do asserts 61000 not 661000), and a session that ends without a capture folds nothing and does not bump sessions_folded (_fold_finished_session returns base unchanged when latest is None; test_a_session_that_captured_nothing_is_not_counted_as_folded asserts sessions_folded==0). One divergence from criterion 1's literal wording: the carry does NOT record which session ids it folded; RuntimeCarry still carries only an integer sessions_folded, and double-counting is prevented by the re-origin mechanism rather than by a folded-session set. That mechanism is sound (within-session counters are monotonic, so re-originating the baseline forward never re-folds already-counted runtime), but sessions_folded counts stints, not distinct sessions, so a deeper interleave (A->B->A->B) increments it per transition and can over-report distinct sessions folded. This is an audit-trail inaccuracy, not a runtime double-count, so it is a followup rather than a blocker. Verified against source and by tracing every added test against the implementation; test outcomes are inferred from the code+test trace (gates not re-run per the working-tree rule).
